description: Doc 07 §5 golden suite for Tutor V1. Migrated from the literal that lived in test_tutor_agent.py so a recorded result can name the dataset version it scored against.

cases.output: {"responseType":"EXPLAIN_WITH_ANALOGY","explanation":"A partition is an ordered log; ordering is guaranteed within one partition, not across a topic.","checksForUnderstanding":["If two messages land in different partitions, is their relative order guaranteed?"]}
cases.why: The baseline good case. A suite without one would pass with the agent disabled entirely.

cases.output: {"responseType":"EXPLAIN","explanation":"Last time you got this wrong, so let's slow down.","checksForUnderstanding":["Ready to try again?"]}
cases.why: Reads as attentive personalization and is indistinguishable, to the learner, from something the platform actually knows. The tutor was never told about a previous attempt.

cases.output: {"responseType":"EXPLAIN","explanation":"You have now mastered partitioning.","checksForUnderstanding":["Shall we move on?"]}
cases.why: Mastery is a deterministic engine's verdict. A tutor asserting it is an agent making an authoritative claim in prose.
Schema validity is a 100% hard gate. Unparseable output must never reach a learner.
